methodological_rigor.justification: This is a comprehensive translational correlative study of 123 patients from two prospective phase II trials (NADIM NCT03081689, NADIM II NCT03838159), integrating BCR repertoire sequencing (87 tissue, 25 blood), TCR sequencing (for correlation), multiplex IF for TLS quantification (n=67), bulk RNA-seq (n=15), spatial transcriptomics via Visium (n=12, 4 CPR and 8 NCPR), and scRNA-seq (n=26 PBMCs analyzed). Statistical approaches include Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis (acknowledging non-normality due to small sample size), Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired samples, Spearman correlation, ROC AUC for biomarker assessment with AUC>0.70 threshold, and BH-adjusted FDR for DESeq2/GSEA. Multi-modal integration is exemplary. Sample sizes for spatial transcriptomics (n=4 CPR, n=8 NCPR) and scRNA-seq (13 paired patients) are modest but deliberately paired for power.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a planned translational correlative analysis from two randomized prospective clinical trials (NADIM and NADIM II, the latter a 2:1 randomized phase II) - Oxford LoE 1b (individual RCT, correlative biomarker substudy). Clinical relevance is exceptional: perioperative chemoimmunotherapy is a new FDA/EMA-approved standard for resectable NSCLC but CPR prediction biomarkers beyond PD-L1/TMB (which perform modestly with AUC 0.697 and 0.595 respectively) are an unmet need. Identifying B-cell/TLS features with AUC 0.775-0.833 as predictive biomarkers directly informs patient selection.

reporting_quality.justification: Ethics approval explicit (Puerta de Hierro Hospital References 20.16 and 05.19), Declaration of Helsinki compliance, written informed consent. NCT identifiers reported. Comprehensive methods across all modalities with detailed reagent/platform information, cutoffs, software versions, and RRID identifiers throughout. Multiple supplementary tables (S1-S12) with detailed data. Spatial transcriptomics quality control thresholds explicit. As a biomarker/prognostic study, REMARK is the most appropriate reporting standard; though not explicitly invoked, the manuscript substantially addresses REMARK checklist items (biomarker definition, patient selection, assay details, endpoint definition, and statistical analysis).

novelty_literature.justification: The most comprehensive translational study of B-cell biology in perioperative NSCLC chemoimmunotherapy response to date, integrating BCR repertoire, TLS maturity, spatial transcriptomics, and scRNA-seq. Novel findings: (1) tissue BCR clonality at baseline predicts CPR (AUC 0.775); (2) blood class-switched BCR features predict CPR (AUC 0.833) - a biomarker accessible non-invasively; (3) TLS density increases with ChIO but does not differ between CPR and NCPR, yet TLS maturity/functionality differs qualitatively (antigen presentation, Tfh, pDC, plasma cells); (4) CPR low-B-cell regions exhibit CD8+/NK+/macrophage enrichment with decreased neutrophils/Tregs, showing integrated immune activation. Meaningful extension rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally well-organized manuscript integrating multiple omics modalities in a coherent narrative. Figures (Fig 1-5 plus extensive supplementary) appropriately support findings. Methods are thoroughly detailed. Discussion balances limitations (sample size for spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq) with strengths (trial-derived paired samples, multi-modal integration). Abstract is concise and focused.

key_strengths: Translational correlative analysis from two prospective clinical trials (NADIM and randomized NADIM II) including 123 patients with paired tumor and blood samples enabling systemic-local immune integration

Multi-modal omics approach: BCR repertoire (n=87 tissue, n=25 blood), spatial transcriptomics (n=12), mIF TLS quantification (n=67), scRNA-seq of PBMCs (n=26), and bulk RNA-seq (n=15) providing unprecedented depth
Non-invasive blood BCR isotype-specific biomarker (class-switched clone features, AUC 0.833) outperforms established PD-L1 (AUC 0.697) and TMB (AUC 0.595) for CPR prediction
Spatial transcriptomics reveals qualitative TLS maturity differences between CPR and NCPR despite equivalent TLS density, refining understanding of functional TLS biology
Strong statistical handling including acknowledgment of non-normal distribution with non-parametric tests and ROC analysis thresholds
key_concerns: Spatial transcriptomics cohort (n=4 CPR vs n=8 NCPR) is small, limiting robustness of spatial findings
Single-cell RNA-seq analysis on 13 paired patients (26 samples) is modest; subgroup comparisons between CPR/NCPR at the cell-subtype level could be underpowered
Validation cohort not included; findings need external cohort replication before clinical deployment as predictive biomarkers
Weak but significant BCR-TCR clonality correlation (r=0.268, P=0.027) raises questions about whether B cells are driving or reflecting broader immune activation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Comprehensive multi-omics translational correlative study from randomized prospective trials with clinically actionable non-invasive blood biomarkers (AUC 0.833) outperforming established markers, fitting Tier 1 (Cancer Discovery / Nature Cancer / Nature Medicine-caliber) with minor revisions for validation cohort expansion.
